requested_operation: separate strict, preservation, recovery, and explicit upgrade semantics so ordinary notebook I/O cannot synthesize fields, relabel versions, or rewrite cell IDs silently

inputs.root_cause: The production reader and writer inherited alpha normalization: load inserted absent metadata, sources, outputs, execution counts, and IDs, while save silently changed the declared minor to 4.5 and regenerated IDs. Consequently preservation mode was not lossless, absent and explicit defaults were indistinguishable, and repeated runs could appear consistent only because every run repeated the same unauthorized rewrite.
inputs.affected_layer: IPYNB lifecycle reader, writer, model reports, and public API

defect_reproduction.outcome: The failure-first lifecycle test could not import upgrade; characterization also showed load() synthesized IDs and dumps() silently relabeled 4.4 input as 4.5.

implementation.mode_boundary: strict validates required current-profile structure without mutation; preservation retains safe unknown and absent values exactly; recovery applies only a documented deterministic repair catalog and records every repair.
implementation.version_identity: IpynbDocument exposes immutable declared_version and detected_version values separately, including an absent declared minor before recovery.
implementation.diagnostics: Parse failures now expose stable codes and logical paths through the public FormatFactoryError context contract.
implementation.explicit_conversion: upgrade() is the only production path that changes the declared version or synthesizes IDs; it returns a conversion action ledger and per-cell rewrite records.
implementation.writer: The declared profile is lossless; the default 4.5 writer refuses a mismatched declared version and requires explicit upgrade. It no longer inserts missing fields or IDs.
implementation.compatibility: The pre-1.0 alpha load_ipynb/write_ipynb facades retain their characterized normalization behavior while the production namespace adopts the durable contract.
implementation.scope_limit: Downgrades remain rejected pending the separate loss-report implementation; no silent downgrade or completion claim was introduced.
